_comment: Physical layout, in millimetres. diagram.json says what is connected; this file says where it physically sits, and form says what the shell is made of. A duck, not a box: a plump egg body, a round head raised at the front, a broad flat orange bill, eyes above it, folded wings on the flanks, a tail at the back and webbed feet under the bill. The dome's footprint matches the body at the parting line, so there is no flat ledge ringing the top (that ledge was what made earlier versions read as a tray). The SDF is the single source of truth; manifold-3d only meshes it for the preview.

blobs._why: the body: an egg whose equator sits a little above the parting line, so at z=26 it is just inside the base footprint (no ledge, no overhang) and the two shells meet flush. The low equator keeps the chest full height where the sonar lives.
the head: a round ball sitting on the front of the body, the way a rubber duck is built - body egg, then head ball, then bill

cav._why: a square hollow at the chest so the 45x20x15 sonar fits on its shelf without the belly curve stealing room

features._why: the bill: a broad flat paddle on the front of the head, orange, protruding forward
left eye, above the bill, welded to the face
tail: a short up-tilted wedge at the back
left wing, a flat ridge folded along the body side
left webbed foot, orange, flat at the bottom front, kept on the bed

parts._why: lying flat on the floor, USB end against the front wall
the bill, standing on the shelf at chest height: far enough back that its 45 mm width is inside the body's full width, looking forward through the cut-outs
rests on top of the sonar, lens turned from +z to -y so it looks forward
the voice, on the floor in the left strip, clear of the rounded corners
x180 points the horn down, out through a slot in the floor
flat on the floor, right side

shelves._why: holds the sonar at bill height, facing the front wall

bosses._why: back-right, clear of the right servo
